memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: No one born of a forbidden marriage nor any of their descendants may enter the assembly of the Lord, not even in the tenth generation. No Ammonite or Moabite or any of their descendants may enter the assembly of the Lord, not even in the tenth generation. - Deut 23:2-3 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
These verses list groups excluded from the assembly, including those of certain births and the Ammonites and Moabites. Again, this is difficult to read, and we must handle it honestly. Under the old covenant, these exclusions guarded Israel's distinct identity and worship, particularly against nations with a history of hostility and idolatry toward God's people.

Yet even within the Old Testament, we glimpse God's grace breaking through these boundaries. Ruth was a Moabite woman, and by all appearance she stood outside the covenant community. But through her faith and God's mercy, she was not only welcomed but became the great-grandmother of King David, and part of the very family line of Jesus the Messiah (Matt 1:5). God's grace reached across the barrier.

This tells us something wonderful. God's mercy is greater than our background, our birth, or our past. No one is beyond the reach of His grace. In Christ, the dividing walls between peoples are broken down, and all who come to Him by faith are welcomed as full members of God's family (Gal 3:28-29). Whatever your history, whatever labels others might place on you, the gospel declares that in Christ you can belong fully to God. Ruth's story reminds us that God delights to bring outsiders in. Is there anything in your past that makes you feel disqualified from God's love? In Christ, grace is greater still.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Does anything in your past make you feel disqualified?
2. How does Ruth's story reveal God's reaching grace?
3. What does full belonging in Christ mean to you?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, thank You that Your grace is greater than my past. Like Ruth, I come as I am and find welcome in Your family through Christ. Amen.
